rationale: Lycopolitan transliteration of Greek ὑδροχόος 'water-pourer' = the zodiac sign Aquarius. The ⲍ-onset for ζ is dialectal; the ⲏ for unstressed o is also Lycopolitan. Used in the cosmic body-zodiac correspondence schema.
Greek ἰχθύς 'fish' = the zodiac sign Pisces. Standard zodiacal term in Manichaean cosmography.

Greek δημιουργός 'craftsman, fashioner.' Manichaean technical term for the dark cosmic fashioner of the human body. Distinct from ⲡⲗⲁⲥⲧⲏⲥ 'molder' and ⲣⲉϩⲣ̄ⲁⲡⲉ 'foreman' — names the archonic body-fashioner specifically.
Reduplicated form of ϣⲱϣ 'scatter, divide' with 3pl object. The cosmogonic act of dispersing the archons within the body in mutual conflict.

Greek οἶκος 'house' used here as a counting-unit: archons distributed 'four by four according to house' (ⲕⲁⲧⲁ ⲟⲓⲕⲟⲥ), with the total number of houses given as 210 myriads. Standard astrological-cosmological 'house' may also be operative given the zodiacal context.
Greek ἀριθμός. Already in accumulated vocabulary; this confirms the technical numerical-cosmological usage.
Compound ⲣ̄- ('do/undergo') + ⲓ̈ϩⲧ. Possibly Lycopolitan for ⲉⲓϩⲧ̄ 'be struck.' Used in punitive-suffering sequence with 'stripe and blow.' Tentative.
Compound: ⲙⲟⲩ ('water') + ⲛ̄- (genitive) + ϩⲙⲟⲩ ('salt'). Lycopolitan ⲍ for ϩ. The flow of saltwater poured forth from the wound — bodily-fluid imagery in the medical-pathological description.

proposed_english: water of defilement / fluid of corruption
rationale: Compound: ⲙⲟⲩ ('water') + ⲛ̄- (genitive) + ⲭⲱⲍⲙⲉ (= ϫⲱϩⲙ̄ 'defilement,' already in glossary as ⲡⲧⲭⲱⲍⲙⲉ). Pus or corrupted bodily fluid in the medical-cosmological pairing with saltwater.
Greek πληγή 'blow, stroke, wound.' Standard medical-pathological term, already attested in vocabulary as ⲡⲗⲏⲣⲏ. Here in the form ⲡⲗⲏⲅⲏ preserving the original spelling.

Indefinite article + ϣⲃⲁ (Lyc. for ϣⲃ̄ⲃⲏⲩⲉ 'exchange, change') — likely 'an exchange/substitution' of treatments. Possibly a technical medical term for the application of a remedy in place of the suffering.
Reduplicated form related to ⲕⲱϩⲕⲉϩ 'scrape.' Medical-surgical treatment in the wound-care sequence (followed by Greek θεραπεύω 'apply therapy').
Verb in medical-treatment context governing ⲁⲃⲁⲗ 'forth.' Tentative reading as a healing/easing verb; the directional 'out' suggests expulsion of the wound-cause from where it entered.

Verbal noun from ⲥⲱⲟⲩϩ 'gather' + ⲁⲍⲟⲩⲛ 'inward.' Already related forms in glossary (ⲣⲉϩⲥⲱⲩⲍ ⲁⲍⲟⲩⲛ 'the Gatherer-Inward'). Chapter-heading technical term for the Manichaean cosmological doctrine of how each element returns inward to its primordial source.
